trial_court: Family Court, Rourkela (C.P. No. 82 of 2011 and C.P.No.216 of 2011)
facts_of_case: The petitioner-wife married the opposite party on 11.03.2011 but the marriage was not consummated due to burn injury detected by the husband. The wife filed for restitution of conjugal rights, which was dismissed, while the husband's petition for nullity was allowed.

legal_principles.principle: An order of interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Act is not a final determination and does contemplate a summary enquiry.
legal_principles.held: The provision clearly provides that the Court may order for maintenance pendent lite in any proceeding under the Act.
cited_cases: Smt Chand Dhawan Vrs. Jawaharlal Dhawan, (1993) SCC (3) 406

legal_principles.principle: The claim for maintenance pendente lite is durated on the pendency of a litigation of the kind envisaged under sections 9 to 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Her claim to permanent maintenance is based on the supposition that either her marital status has been strained or affected by passing a decree for restitution of conjugal rights or judicial separation in favour or against her, or her marriage stands dissolved by a decree of nullity or divorce, with or without her consent.
cited_cases: Smt Chand Dhawan Vrs. Jawaharlal Dhawan, (1993) SCC (3) 406

legal_principles.principle: An order of interim maintenance can be made at the outset without much contest.
legal_principles.held: The above judgment is reiterated in Ramesh Chandra Rampratapji Daga case (supra).
cited_cases: Ramesh Chandra Rampratapji Daga Vrs. Ramemshwari Ramesh Chandra Daga, AIR 2005 SC 422

legal_principles.principle: No distinction has been made under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act relating to right of a wife for maintenance in case preferred under sections 12 or 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: So far as maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceeding are concerned no distinction has been made under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act relating to right of a wife for maintenance in case preferred under sections 12 or 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
cited_cases: Sandeep Kuar @ Bobby Vrs. The State of Jharkhand and Anr., AIR 2004 Jharkhand 22

outcome.final_order: The final court order granted the petitioner-wife interim maintenance of Rs.10,000 per month.
